message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's morally acceptable for me to refuse to cover my co-worker's shift so he can attend his sister's memorial. Let me break this down step by step. First, my co-worker asked me to cover his shift from 2pm to 10pm, or maybe 3pm to 10pm. He needs to do this because his sister passed away, and he wants to attend her memorial. I don't know the exact details of when his sister died, but I do know that our work schedules are set a week in advance every Tuesday. That means he knew about his shift at least a week before he asked me to cover it. Our workplace has a system where employees can request to work only part of their shift and have someone else cover the rest. This is done through an online employee attendance system. My co-worker submitted a partial shift request, but no one was available to cover him. So, he started texting people, including me, to see if they could come in and cover his shift. I absolutely hate this job, so when he asked me, I said I couldn't come in, even though I was free. He's asked me before to cover his shifts, and I did it once. I also asked him to cover one of my shifts later, thinking we were even in terms of favors. After I declined his request, he texted me back saying, "Of course not," which made me feel like an asshole. Now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole here. Let me think about the different aspects of this situation. On one hand, my co-worker is going through a tough time because his sister passed away. Attending her memorial is important for him to grieve and say goodbye. On the other hand, I hate my job and don't want to put in extra hours, especially for someone who has asked me before. I also consider the fact that he knew about his shift a week in advance. If he knew he needed to attend his sister's memorial, why didn't he make arrangements earlier? Maybe he didn't know when the memorial was scheduled until closer to the date. Or perhaps he assumed someone else would cover his shift, but no one was available. I also think about the system in place at work. There's an online system for requesting partial shifts and finding someone to cover. If no one was available through that system, he had to ask people manually. That seems reasonable because the system didn't work for him. I also feel that I've covered his shift once before, and I asked him to cover mine later. So, in a way, we were balancing the favors. But he didn't cover my shift, and now I'm being asked again. Maybe I feel like I'm not getting my end of the deal, so I'm hesitant to help him again. Another thing to consider is the emotional aspect. My co-worker is grieving, and I can understand why he needs to attend his sister's memorial. But I also have my own feelings about the job and my time. It's a tough spot to be in because I want to be supportive, but I also don't want to be taken advantage of. I also wonder about the workplace culture. If everyone only covers shifts when it's convenient for them, does that create a problematic environment? Or is it reasonable to expect some flexibility, especially in times of personal need? In the end, I'm torn between being a supportive colleague and taking care of my own well-being and job satisfaction. I need to decide whether refusing to cover his shift in this situation is morally acceptable or not.
